entry.title: Disenfranchisement in Spatial Voting Games
entry.summary:
The questions of voting rights, group membership, and the boundaries of acceptable discourse all involve a recursive, self-stability issue, wherein the voters, group members, and acceptable commentators are often the ultimate arbiters of their own rules for inclusion and exclusion. In order to understand how ideological or issue diversity may impact the stability of such inclusion and exclusion, we introduce franchise elections, where voting members of a group vote to change the electorate. In particular, when agents are positioned inside an ideological or issue space, a social choice function that aggregates agent viewpoints induces a preference for agents over group composition, where agents prefer groups that improve the social choice function outcome for them.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #decision-theory #market-design

entry.title: Learning Dynamics of the Influencer's Game in Resource Landscapes
entry.summary:
Across domains as varied as ecology, economics, and online platforms, individuals are incentivized to position themselves within resource-rich strategy spaces. In this work we introduce a new spatial game framework called the influencer's game. Within this new framework players' strategies are represented as positions within a trait space.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #decision-theory #market-design

entry.title: Accuracy Is Not Welfare: Evaluating AI Buyers under Strategic Price Complexity in a Synthetic Duopoly
entry.summary:
AI buying agents may alter sellers' incentives as well as consumers' decisions. In a synthetic duopoly, we evaluate price-comparison pipelines on a fixed menu and in empirical correlated-equilibrium games. Calculator assistance selects an optimal offer 84.00% of the time, versus 68.57% under verified-total disclosure, yet disclosure has a 20.14-unit higher consumer-worst equilibrium surplus.

Source: arXiv Economics (econ.EM, econ.GN, econ.TH) · Tags: #econometrics #macroeconomics #decision-theory #quant-finance

entry.title: A systematic comparison of physics-informed neural networks and mechanistic models for epidemic modeling and forecasting
entry.summary:
Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have recently been applied to epidemic modeling and forecasting with promising results. These methods integrate mechanistic knowledge with data-driven learning. Yet, their comparative performance against well-established, and simpler epidemic models is underexplored.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #ml-theory #neuroscience

entry.title: The directions of science: How we search the unknown
entry.summary:
Science is producing knowledge at unprecedented scale, while artificial intelligence promises to accelerate the generation of hypotheses, analyses, and scientific outputs further. Yet increasing the volume of research does not necessarily expand the range of directions science effectively explores. We argue that science can be understood as a collective search process in which finite resources are allocated across an evolving space of possible research trajectories.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems

entry.title: Go under Chinese Rules with a Succinct Game History is Complete for Exponential Space
entry.summary:
The complexity of games is a central topic in combinatorics, algorithms, and computational complexity theory. It asks how difficult it is to determine the winner of a combinatorial game under optimal play. Many games, such as Hex or Othello, are PSPACE-complete: the game tree has polynomial depth, so the game can be decided in PSPACE.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #algorithms

entry.title: Latent resonances in oscillator networks
entry.summary:
In networks of coupled oscillators, from neural circuits to power grids, damping is expected to suppress oscillations because of its dissipativity. Here we show that local damping can, counterintuitively, amplify oscillations along some input-output channels, while the network's global oscillation energy decreases and its spectral properties improve. The amplified oscillation arises from a latent resonance that lies in the spectrum yet barely manifests.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #neuroscience

entry.title: Emulating spatially extended systems using Fourier Neural Operator
entry.summary:
Operator Learning (OL) algorithms approximate underlying mathematical operators by mapping entire classes of input functions to their corresponding solutions. For instance, architectures such as the Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) have been trained on numerical datasets generated by isolated, stiff ionic models to provide a data-driven alternative to traditional numerical integration schemes. However, real-world biological and physical systems typically consist of interconnected spatial units arranged in complex, heterogeneous networks.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #combinatorics #neuroscience

entry.title: Indefinite causal order with definite Bohmian trajectories for the quantum switch
entry.summary:
We analyze the notion of indefinite causal order (ICO) from the standpoint of the deterministic de Broglie--Bohm theory, based on the notion of trajectories in configuration space. More precisely, we study the physics of the quantum switch (QS) interferometer within a Bohmian framework and show how the notion of causality is preserved in this approach. Furthermore, we investigate device-independent certification and causal inequalities applied to an entangled quantum system, and show that in this regime too, the notions of trajectories and of a strict causal order are perfectly preserved.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #quantum-computing

entry.title: Spatial scaling of heterogeneity transfer from boron concentration to absorbed dose in boron neutron capture therapy
entry.summary:
We investigate how the amplitude and spatial correlation length of boron-concentration fluctuations affect the boron-induced absorbed-dose distribution in boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT). The spatial energy-deposition response of alpha particles and lithium nuclei is obtained using Geant4 and convolved with three-dimensional correlated lognormal boron fields under a uniform neutron field. Approximately $90\%$ of the reaction-product energy is deposited within a radius of $6.00~μ\mathrm{m}$, with a characteristic deposition length of $\ell_B\approx2.05~μ\mathrm{m}$.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems

entry.title: The Tournament Equilibrium Set Is PSPACE-Complete, Even under Hereditary Uniqueness
entry.summary:
The tournament equilibrium set (TEQ), proposed by Schwartz in 1990, is a classical voting rule based on pairwise majority comparisons. Its definition is recursive: an alternative is judged by the alternatives that beat it, called its dominators, and by which of those dominators TEQ itself selects. Deciding whether a given alternative belongs to TEQ was known to be NP-hard and to lie in PSPACE.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #algorithms

entry.title: The Submodular Secretary Problem: Tight $1-1/e$ for Monotone Objectives, and Strictly Between $1/e$ and $1/2$ in General
entry.summary:
In the submodular secretary problem with a cardinality constraint, $n$ elements arrive in uniformly random order, and an algorithm must irrevocably accept or reject each one on arrival so as to maximize a nonnegative submodular function over sets of at most $k$ elements. For monotone objectives we settle the problem: the optimal competitive ratio tends to exactly $1-1/e$ as $k\to\infty$, and its worst case over all budgets $k$ is exactly $1/e$. The bound $1-1/e$ cannot be exceeded even with unlimited computation, and it is achieved by a single algorithm with at most $4n+1$ value queries; previously the best ratio without a shortlist was $1/e-o(1)$, with exponentially many queries.

Source: arXiv Game Theory, Complex Systems & Soc-Phys (cs.GT, nlin.AO, physics.soc-ph) · Tags: #decision-theory #complex-systems #algorithms
